info.title: TRUE Connector API
info.description: Authenticate with `POST /api/v1/auth/login`, then use **Authorize** to provide the returned JWT with the `bearerAuth` scheme. Use an `ADMIN` token for management endpoints and a `CONNECTOR` token for tenant-scoped DSP protocol endpoints.

tags.name: Catalog
tags.description: Manage the provider catalog and its relationships to datasets, distributions, and data services.

tags.name: Dataset
tags.description: Manage DCAT datasets, their policies and distributions, and their associated file or external artifacts.

tags.name: Distribution
tags.description: Manage DCAT distributions that describe how a dataset is made available through a data service.

tags.name: Data Service
tags.description: Manage the DCAT data services referenced by catalog distributions.

tags.name: Agreement
tags.description: Evaluate policy constraints for an existing contract agreement.

tags.name: Transfer
tags.description: Manage transfer processes. A valid agreement is required before a transfer is requested. The process moves from INITIALIZED to REQUESTED to STARTED, may be suspended and restarted, and finishes as COMPLETED or TERMINATED. HTTP_PULL gives the consumer a provider artifact endpoint; HTTP_PUSH lets the provider write to the consumer's destination using temporary credentials.

tags.name: Application Properties
tags.description: Read and update runtime application properties.

tags.name: Artifact
tags.description: Retrieve artifact metadata associated with catalog datasets.

tags.name: Audit Events
tags.description: Browse tenant-scoped audit events and event types.

tags.name: Authentication
tags.description: The unified login, refresh, and logout API is permit-all in INTERNAL and KEYCLOAK modes. INTERNAL validates credentials against MongoDB and issues connector JWTs; KEYCLOAK delegates the same contract to Keycloak.

tags.name: Contract negotiation
tags.description: Manage negotiations as either consumer or provider. The state machine progresses through REQUESTED, OFFERED, ACCEPTED, AGREED, VERIFIED, and FINALIZED, with TERMINATED available from intermediate states. Actual transitions depend on the current state: REQUESTED may become OFFERED, AGREED, or TERMINATED; OFFERED may return to REQUESTED, become ACCEPTED, or terminate; ACCEPTED may become AGREED or terminate; AGREED may become VERIFIED or terminate; VERIFIED may become FINALIZED or terminate.

tags.name: Dashboard Metrics
tags.description: Retrieve operational metrics for the authenticated user's tenant context.

tags.name: Proxy
tags.description: Forward catalog and dataset-format lookups to a configured provider.

tags.name: Tenants
tags.description: Manage tenant lifecycle and configuration. All tenant operations require ROLE_SUPER_ADMIN. Each tenant has isolated management/protocol data and its own S3 bucket. For other tenant-scoped management APIs, a super-admin can pass X-Tenant-Id to scope a request to one tenant; without it, super-admin requests are not tenant-scoped. A regular tenant admin uses the tenant in their authenticated identity and cannot override it with this header.

tags.name: Users
tags.description: Manage INTERNAL-mode users. Most user operations require ROLE_SUPER_ADMIN. ROLE_ADMIN may read /me and change their own password; the service verifies ownership. The updateNames operation currently remains protected by the ROLE_SUPER_ADMIN users rule. UserAPIController is inactive in KEYCLOAK mode, where KeycloakUserApiController exposes read-only user listing and user creation or updates are managed in Keycloak. User list results exclude ROLE_CONNECTOR accounts. New passwords must be 8 to 16 characters and contain at least one lowercase letter, uppercase letter, digit, and special character.

get.description: Return a user by ID. This cross-user lookup requires ROLE_SUPER_ADMIN; ROLE_ADMIN access is limited to the current-user and own-password self-service routes.

parameters.name: X-Tenant-Id

put.description: Change a user's first and last name. The service checks that non-super-admin callers target their own account, but this route is currently protected by the broad ROLE_SUPER_ADMIN users rule; the ROLE_ADMIN security exception applies to /me and /{id}/password.

put.description: Change the target user's password after verifying the current password. ROLE_ADMIN may use this only for their own account; ROLE_SUPER_ADMIN may change any user's password. The new password must be 8 to 16 characters and include a lowercase letter, uppercase letter, digit, and special character.

put.description: Send a TransferTerminationMessage to the counterparty and record TERMINATED after a successful response. Temporary HTTP_PUSH bucket credentials are cleaned up after the termination succeeds.

parameters.name: X-Tenant-Id

put.description: Start a transfer process. The provider sends a TransferStartMessage to the consumer; for HTTP_PULL the message includes the provider artifact endpoint (a presigned S3 URL for FILE artifacts or the connector artifact endpoint for EXTERNAL artifacts). A consumer cannot start a transfer that is still REQUESTED. STARTED is persisted after the peer acknowledges the message.

put.description: Send a TransferCompletionMessage to the counterparty and record COMPLETED after a successful response. The process must be in a state that permits completion; data download and policy checks are handled by the consumer download/view flow.

put.description: Verify the agreed contract as the consumer. The connector sends a ContractAgreementVerificationMessage to the provider and records VERIFIED only after the provider responds successfully.

parameters.name: X-Tenant-Id
parameters.description: Optional tenant identifier used by super-admin requests to scope management operations.

put.description: Terminate an existing negotiation from either participant role. The connector sends a ContractNegotiationTerminationMessage to the counterparty callback, then records TERMINATED after success.

parameters.name: X-Tenant-Id
parameters.description: Optional tenant identifier used by super-admin requests to scope management operations.

put.description: Send a revised offer for an existing negotiation. The connector validates the offer, sends a ContractRequestMessage to the provider callback, and updates the stored negotiation when the peer accepts it.

parameters.name: X-Tenant-Id
parameters.description: Optional tenant identifier used by super-admin requests to scope management operations.

put.description: Send a revised offer to the consumer for an existing negotiation. The connector validates the offer and current transition, sends a ContractOfferMessage to the consumer callback, and updates the stored offer and negotiation after a successful response.

parameters.name: X-Tenant-Id
parameters.description: Optional tenant identifier used by super-admin requests to scope management operations.

put.description: Finalize a verified negotiation as provider. The connector sends a ContractNegotiationEventMessage with event type FINALIZED to the consumer, records FINALIZED after a successful callback, and initializes the transfer process for the resulting agreement. The endpoint returns a success response rather than the updated negotiation.

parameters.name: X-Tenant-Id
parameters.description: Optional tenant identifier used by super-admin requests to scope management operations.

put.description: Agree to the negotiation as provider. The connector derives an Agreement from the current offer, sends a ContractAgreementMessage to the consumer, and saves the agreement and AGREED negotiation state after a successful callback response.

parameters.name: X-Tenant-Id
parameters.description: Optional tenant identifier used by super-admin requests to scope management operations.

put.description: Accept the current offer as the consumer. The connector sends a ContractNegotiationEventMessage with event type ACCEPTED to the provider and records ACCEPTED after a successful callback response.

post.description: Initiate a transfer for an existing transfer process linked to a negotiated agreement. The consumer sends the selected wire format (HttpData-PULL or HttpData-PUSH; internal names HTTP_PULL and HTTP_PUSH) to the provider and records REQUESTED after a successful response. HTTP_PUSH provisions temporary write credentials and includes the consumer destination address; HTTP_PULL leaves artifact retrieval to the consumer using the provider endpoint supplied when the transfer starts.

HTTP_PUSH sends the artifact directly from the provider to the consumer's S3 destination and does not use this download step. The endpoint returns an accepted JSON response while a download runs.
